:::{#cor-gram-invertible-iff}
#### $\tp{\mX}\mX$ is invertible exactly when $\mX$ has full column rank

For an $n \times p$ matrix $\mX$, the $p \times p$ matrix $\tp{\mX}\mX$ is invertible (@def-invertible-matrix)
exactly when $\operatorname{rank}(\mX) = p$ (@def-full-column-rank).

:::

::: proof

The following statements are equivalent:

$$
\ba
\tp{\mX}\mX \text{ is invertible}
&\iff \mathcal{N}(\tp{\mX}\mX) = \cb{\vzero_p}
&& \text{(@thm-invertible-rank)}
\\
&\iff \mathcal{N}(\mX) = \cb{\vzero_p}
&& \text{(@thm-null-gram)}
\\
&\iff \mX \text{ has full column rank.}
&& \text{(@thm-independent-null-space)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-gram-invertible-iff}
#### A design matrix with a repeated column

$\mX = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ of @exm-rank has rank $1 < 2$.
Its cross-product matrix is

$$
\tp{\mX}\mX = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 6 \\ 6 & 12 \end{bmatrix},
$$

which is singular: $(2, -1)$ is in its null space,
because $\mX (2, -1) = \vzero_3$ (@exm-independent-null-space).
For the full-column-rank matrix of @exm-gram-invertible, $\tp{\mX}\mX$ is invertible.

:::
